title: Qualify inbound leads and route them to your CRM
summary: Score each inbound form or email against your criteria, pick a CRM stage, and draft one short qualifying follow-up. You approve before anything sends.

tests.prompt:
A new lead just came in. Score them against my criteria and draft one follow-up email.

Lead details: [NAME], [COMPANY], [WHAT THEY ASKED FOR / FORM MESSAGE], [SOURCE], [EMAIL if known].
My business: [ONE-LINE DESCRIPTION], [MAIN OFFER], [IDEAL CUSTOMER — e.g. company size, budget, timeline].
Qualify criteria: [LIST 3–5 MUST-HAVES AND NICE-TO-HAVES].

Output in this order:
1) Fit: Good / Maybe / Poor — one sentence why.
2) Suggested CRM stage: [STAGE NAME OPTIONS YOU USE].
3) One follow-up email under 100 words that references what they asked for and asks exactly one qualifying question (budget, timeline, or size — pick the most relevant).
4) Fields to save: name, company, request summary, source, fit, stage.

Do not invent facts about the lead. If the form is thin, say so and ask the one question that would help most.

setup.agent: n8n, Make, or Zapier plus your CRM (e.g. HubSpot)
steps: Trigger on a new form submission or labeled inbound email.
Pass lead fields and your qualify criteria into the prompt.
Create or update the CRM contact with fit, stage, and request summary.
Attach the drafted email as a task or email draft.
Notify yourself in Slack or SMS to approve before send.
setup.approvalStep: The follow-up stays a draft until you approve it. Spam and test leads are discarded by you, not auto-sent.
failureModes: Generic emails when the form message is empty
Asking more than one qualifying question
Creating CRM records for spam or test submissions

toolPicks.why: Forms, stages, and free CRM in one place.
toolPicks.whenNot: You already have a CRM you like.
High volume where per-task pricing hurts.

faq.a: Not at first. Review drafts for a week, then auto-send only lead types you always approve.

faq.q: What if the request is vague?
faq.a: Mark fit as Maybe and ask one clear question. Improve the form later so new leads arrive with more context.
